flawed_step: 0018-0019: For odd m, the roots of X^2+sqrt(5)X+1 are (-sqrt(5)±1)/2, namely -phi and -phi^{-1}, not -phi and phi^{-1}.
counterexample: Take p=7 and m=55. Explicitly, F_54=86267571272=49·1760562679+1 and F_55=139583862445=49·2848650254-1, so F_55≡-1 (mod 49). Work in R=(Z/49Z)[s]/(s^2-5), with phi=(1+s)/2. Since phi^m=F_m phi+F_{m-1}, phi^55≡-phi+1=1-phi=-phi^{-1}. This is not -phi (their difference is 1) and not phi^{-1}=phi-1 (their difference is 1-s, which is nonzero in R). Thus the claimed alternatives in 0018-0019 fail concretely.
assessment_summary: The argument is correct through the quadratic in 0015, but its odd-case roots are computed with the wrong signs in 0018-0019. The explicit p=7, m=55 calculation witnesses the failure, so verification stops there.
